name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 241,930 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Low/high allow for the Natural Earth polygon vs official figure and inland water (surface area is a few % larger).

population.note: asOf 2025: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 69,487,000. Everything inside ne:GBR (Great Britain and Northern Ireland); Crown dependencies and overseas territories excluded.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance as quoted: 141,100 active. Low: 137,970 regular forces (MoD statistics April 2026, British Armed Forces article). CIA Factbook 2025: ~138,000 regulars plus 40-45,000 reserves and others on active duty. World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 153,000 (2020).

trainedReserves.note: IISS as quoted: 70,450 reserves (all trained and untrained categories). Low: CIA Factbook 2025 "approximately 40-45,000 reserves" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/europe/uk.json).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 141,100 minus infantry P roles (23,000). Covers navy and air force personnel, armour/artillery/air-defence crews, logistics, staff, training and other support.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to WWII Britain (~5.9 million in uniform from ~48 million, ~12%) scaled down for an all-volunteer force with no conscription law, no stored equipment for mass levies and an older population.

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured and mechanized infantry riflemen: ~6 Warrior/Boxer battalions and 4 heavy protected mobility battalions x ~550-600. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_British_Army)

count.note: Educated guess. Light infantry, Parachute Regiment, Gurkhas and 3 Commando Brigade Royal Marines (~6,000): ~20 battalions x ~500 plus commandos. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_British_Army)

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 3,003,331,701,150 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD x 0.8005) / population 69,487,000 = 43,221. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 3,751,819,739,100 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 3,003,331,701,150 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: 2.35% of GDP in 2025 (mid), 2.44% in 2024, 2.04% in 2021. Low is the lowest of those years; high allows ~5% for NATO-definition spending above SIPRI.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 16.5% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.99. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/GBR/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 0.85% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.69 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.67-0.70). Mid 1 - 0.009/0.69 = 0.99. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.67 = 0.98. High: s 0.70 = 0.99. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 69% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. UK imports ~40% of food; production mostly consumed domestically.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 34,225,295 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 6.304% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 431,535. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Typhoon line at BAE Warton kept open by export orders; F-35 rear fuselages built in the UK but assembled in the US. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_United_Kingdom_military_aircraft)

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Type 26 (Govan) and Type 31 (Rosyth) frigates under construction, about one hull per year each.

armor.note: Educated guess. Challenger 3 conversions at RBSL Telford (148 by 2027).

submarines.note: Educated guess. BAE Barrow builds the last Astutes and Dreadnought SSBNs.

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 424,129 km, all paved (2020); 3,701 km motorway.

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 16,179 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 185 ports, 7 large + 24 medium = 31 (mid); low counts large ports only.

merchantTonnage.note: UNCTAD 2025 as quoted: 10,327 thousand DWT under the UK flag. High is an educated guess for British-owned tonnage under other flags (Isle of Man, Gibraltar, Bermuda red ensign group excluded from mid).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. NATO-standard deployable logistics, A400M/C-17 airlift and RFA sealift; UK planned Op Granby-scale divisional deployment.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026: 120 deployed strategic + 105 reserve = 225 stockpile (mid); low = deployed on Trident II D5. High: the 2021 Integrated Review cap of no more than 260 warheads.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: island with naval moat, familiar terrain, population support; little strategic depth, no harsh-climate bonus.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:GBR (World Bank); overseas territories and Crown dependencies excluded. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from Wikipedia inventory tables (British Army equipment list, active aircraft list with in-service/total columns, July 2026 active ships list) and IISS as quoted; ships_major = carriers/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = OPV, patrol, MCM; drones = Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). No ground-launched missiles; the Trident force is carried by the 4 SSBNs counted under submarines. Army in transition: Challenger 3, Boxer and Ajax replacing older fleets, AS-90 gone, so armour and artillery counts are unusually uncertain for 2026.
